client_brief:
NORTHGROVE: hang-tag run

Project overview
NORTHGROVE is the repeat client for this benchmark series. We are hiring an expert to turn the supplied working files into NORTHGROVE hang-tag run, NORTHGROVE capsule photography, garments and hardware, and NORTHGROVE cut-out set.

What we will provide
northgrove_fw_flatlays/ (10 frames); northgrove_hardware_bench/ (4 frames); kestrel_pennant.jpg; northgrove_hangtag.pdf; northgrove_linesheet.csv; northgrove_copy.txt. Every file must be accounted for in the final manifest; it may be used, retained as reference, superseded, or rejected with a reason.

Scope and deliverables
- NORTHGROVE hang-tag run: Ten hang tags, one record per page, built on last season's approved artwork: one press file whose page count equals the row count in row order for the printer, plus one correctly identified file per piece at genuine print resolution for the buyer pack,...
- NORTHGROVE capsule photography, garments and hardware: Ten garment masters brought to one capsule target across two mornings (one ground, one white point, one warmth, one piece height in frame) plus four hardware masters held to a separate colour-accurate near-white target with true metal tone, plus one...
- NORTHGROVE cut-out set: Fourteen genuine cut-outs, ten garments and four hardware pieces, whole at full resolution on the house colour with shoulder seam, placket and hem intact and no reference card, bench edge or prop surviving into any frame. 

Non-negotiables
- Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
- Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
- Reconcile records before merge and prove page, row, name, and amount completeness from the delivered artifacts.

Working process
Please begin with an inventory and risk pass, submit the first proof or direction at the stated checkpoint, then revise against consolidated feedback. We are hiring for judgment: flag contradictions early, make the strongest defensible choice, and document any source limitation rather than hiding it.

Contract
$3,000-$7,000 fixed; target delivery 2 to 4 weeks; one direction checkpoint and two consolidated revision rounds. Final handoff includes the delivery manifest, editable sources where scoped, final exports, and a concise production note.

Primary: the Freelancer.com background-removal and apparel brief in the ledger, whose literal asks (compositing a second shirt into the scene, AI-erasing room clutter) are both on the connector's not-available list, so the job is honestly re-cast to the apparel-catalog intent the category points at and scaled from a single hero to a capsule workload; the fictional brand NORTHGROVE (olive leaf glyph plus a charcoal condensed wordmark) is that ledger's own coinage. Co-anchor: the Freelancer.com flat-lay apparel brief asking for 'a clean, consistent set of flat-lay photos' shot 'directly overhead, evenly lit' on a 'mid-gray' backdrop that 'keeps dark and light fabrics balanced on screen', plus high-resolution files and web-ready versions. Co-anchor: the Freelancer.com silver-jewellery open call asking for handheld product frames turned into a colour-accurate uniform-white set with 'accurate metal tone', 'no colour cast' and matching transparent cut-outs for layering, absorbed here as the capsule's cast metal hardware, which correctly needs a different treatment from the garments. Co-anchor: the Upwork brand-identity post for an invented amateur league, converted per the rework guidance from cricket to a Western sport, and absorbed as the capsule's collaboration with a fictional local lacrosse club whose only surviving artwork is a photographed pennant. No real company, label, league, club, retailer or trademark is named anywhere. VERDICT STRENGTHEN: the concept and collateral set are kept and deepened to standard, with the merge run added because a hang tag per SKU is genuine record-per-page work that the authoring surface cannot do at print resolution.

price_band_and_audience: Mid-premium heritage workwear at 74 to 128 dollars per piece, buyer 28 to 45, values provenance and construction over logos. The band is load-bearing. At this price the campaign wants muted grounds, full-frame quiet photography that shows cloth and seam, and copy that leads on material and make; the linesheet is a trade document that has to look sober beside a buyer's other lines. The same ten pieces at a 24 dollar fast-fashion band would correctly be a dense grid of cut-outs on white with a burst price and a discount ladder, and shipping that treatment here tells forty independent stockists that the capsule is not what the wholesale price says it is. Push the other way into editorial luxury, vast white space, a tiny mark and no price anywhere, and a buyer cannot work from it and a 74 dollar henley reads as mispriced. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 2,000 to 3,800 dollars fixed.

assets_supplied.name: northgrove_fw_flatlays/ (10 frames)
assets_supplied.kind: Overhead flat-lay photography of the ten capsule pieces on a mid-gray backdrop, shot across two mornings, one piece per frame.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everything shot flat on the gray. The gray keeps the dark pieces and the natural cotton balanced on screen."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The charcoal overshirt and the dark olive henley sit at almost exactly the backdrop's luminance along the shoulder and placket, so a one-call knockout reports success and returns a plausible cut-out that has bitten into the shoulder seam and the placket edge, visible only at full resolution on a coloured ground. Separately the backdrop was re-hung between the two mornings and the second batch sits fractionally warmer, which reads as nothing in a single frame and reads as two shoots the moment the range grid puts them adjacent.

assets_supplied.name: northgrove_hardware_bench/ (4 frames)
assets_supplied.kind: Bench frames of the cast pewter and silver hardware: two button styles, a keyring and a collar pin, shot on a light bench.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The hardware we cast this season. These need true metal tone and no cast."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: One frame has a grey reference card lying in the corner of the bench, and a subject-focused crop on sparse bench art can lock onto the card or onto a specular highlight instead of the piece, returning a confident looking crop at a plausible size while reporting its uncertainty only as a numeric detection confidence and a bounding box buried in the metadata. The metal also carries a cool cast that any global warm move made for the garments pushes further from true, so the two families cannot share one grade.

assets_supplied.name: kestrel_pennant.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of the lacrosse club's wool pennant hanging on a workshop wall, the crest chain-stitched in two thread colours on felt.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only place the club's crest still exists. They let us photograph it off the wall."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a compound stitched mark on a textile substrate, which behaves nothing like a flat scan: a prompt naming the pennant returns the felt rather than the thread, a compound prompt returns the outer ring and silently drops the inner rule and the central device while looking entirely plausible, and the knockout route on the ring returns a solid opaque disc because an enclosed interior cannot be punched. The chain-stitch texture also explodes a trace into far more paths than the mark has parts.

assets_supplied.name: northgrove_hangtag.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: Last season's hang tag as the printer's own press PDF, one tag, double sided, with a placed swatch image and a specification block.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The tag our printer ran last season. Same size and stock this year."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The tag carries no bleed and the converted document carries none either, so a press-ready with bleed promise cannot be met from this source however the render is called, and the specification block is a fixed measure frame that stops rendering rather than spilling when a record overruns it.

assets_supplied.name: northgrove_linesheet.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Ten rows: piece name, fabric, make note, colourway, wholesale and retail price, size run, and a column pointing at the cut-out for each piece.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The ten pieces as our stockists get them. The last column is meant to pull in the picture."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The image column header is written plainly and its cells hold folder-relative paths rather than bare filenames, which binds nothing at merge time while every tool response still reports success, so every tag renders carrying the template's original static swatch and looks like a finished tag.

assets_supplied.name: northgrove_copy.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text: the ten piece names, fabric and make notes, the season statement and the stockist terms.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The copy as we want it read."

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the cut-outs the whole linesheet and tag run depend on are actually whole. The backdrop was chosen precisely because it sits between the dark and the light pieces, and on the charcoal overshirt and the dark olive henley that puts cloth and ground at almost the same luminance along the shoulder and the placket. The knockout returns a clean looking RGBA cut-out with no warning and a full success, and at preview scale against white it looks correct; the bite into the shoulder seam and the placket edge only appears at full resolution against a colour. Which pieces this happens to is a property of each frame's own tonal relationship to the ground and cannot be read off the frame.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it. The knockout has to happen after the grade, and the grade is what fixes the tonal relationship; there is no parameter that reports whether a boundary was found and no read-ahead that says which pieces have one. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the gray keeps the dark and light pieces balanced on screen, which is the client explaining a sound photographic choice, and says the dark pieces are the ones she worries about, which is a worry, not a disclosure. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is a different chain for the affected pieces: select the backdrop by its own material properties, invert and fill so the boundary is drawn rather than detected, or composite onto the house colour in one call so the ground is part of the raster and there is no edge to fail.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-cut the affected pieces through the drawn-boundary route, re-inspect every cut edge at full resolution on the house colour rather than on white, and re-derive the range grid frames and the tag pictures that were already built on the first cut-outs.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A linesheet and a hang-tag run sent to forty stockists in which the two dark pieces have had their shoulder seam and placket eaten away, on a capsule sold on construction, discovered by a buyer.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the tag run actually is once it exists. Three things surface only in the returned artefacts, all at full success. The merge accepts a resolution on its own raster output and silently ignores it, returning page-sized files at screen resolution that open and print and look like proofs. The per-record raster files come back in an order that the response's own row labels contradict, so naming files by their position in the returned list attaches the wrong piece to the wrong name. And the picture column binds nothing in the shape the supplied data file uses, so every tag renders carrying the template's original static swatch and still looks like a finished tag.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and doing it right the first time presumes knowing that a documented parameter is inert, that stated labels are wrong, and that a plainly written data column is the wrong shape, none of which any response says. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for a tag per piece at print resolution carrying that piece's own picture, which is the requirement, not the diagnosis. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is a different delivery route entirely: merge to the document format and render separately for real resolution, and either render as separate files or drive one record at a time so identity is guaranteed by the call rather than inferred from a list, with the data column reshaped so the binding can happen at all.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reshape the picture column and its file references, re-prepare and re-merge, take the raster branch through the render step instead of the merge's own output, re-derive every per-piece file through a route whose identity is guaranteed, and read each delivered tag at trim against its row, where the long make notes will also show whether a fixed measure block stopped rendering rather than spilled.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Ten hang tags sent to the printer at a quarter of the resolution they need, in a buyer pack where the filenames name the wrong pieces, every one of them carrying last season's swatch instead of this season's garment, with every tool response having reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the season's world survives into the lookbook at all. The muted campaign tone over full-frame photography is naturally authored as a tonal layer sitting over the picture, and the importer discards that blending construction outright: the layer arrives as a plain opaque shape, at full success, with no warning, sitting on top of the photograph it was supposed to tint. The returned per-page markup is the only channel that reports it, and the document's own rendition returns the first page only, so a ten-look lookbook and both poster directions cannot be checked visually beyond page one. Whether each look still reads as the capsule's world, or as a flat panel covering a garment, is visible only after the export.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the drop happens at import and the import is the last step; and doing it right the first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no response reports and no checklist enumerates. (b) Nothing states it. The acceptance line about the looks reading as the season's muted world on every page is the client's art direction, not a warning about an importer. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to produce a different upstream asset, with the tone applied to the raster itself in the image pipeline so the layout carries no look it cannot hold, and then to re-judge the page because a baked tone and an overlaid tone do not sit the same way under type.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Take the affected photography back through the image pipeline with the tone applied to the raster, re-author the lookbook and the poster directions around rasters that already carry the look, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and audit every page from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A buyer lookbook delivered in which nine of the ten looks are a flat panel sitting over a garment on the pages nobody looked at, with the export having reported success throughout.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are raster work, which need an authored fixed canvas document, and which are genuine record-per-page variable data with a per-row picture.
Whether the ten flat-lays are one shoot. The client believes the backdrop held; the range grid is the only place that can settle it.
Two grade targets or one. The garments want the capsule's muted world and the metal wants colour accuracy on near-white, and they still have to sit on one linesheet page without fighting.

Knockout route per piece: the one-call route where there is a tonal boundary, versus drawing the boundary through a ground-named selection inverted and filled, or compositing onto the house colour where there is none.
Whether to trust a confident looking crop on sparse bench art or to spend the extra calls on an explicit selection, given that a reference card in a delivered frame is a client-visible failure.

Selection wording on the pennant: naming the pennant takes the felt, naming the thread's own visual properties takes the mark, and the knockout route on an enclosed ring is the wrong instrument entirely.
How much of a chain-stitched trace to keep, given that the stitch texture produces far more parts than the mark has.
Whether the season's tone is carried by the layout or baked into the raster upstream, and what that choice costs if the layout cannot hold it.

acceptance_snapshot: The hardware is colour accurate on near-white with true metal tone and no cast, and it is graded as its own family rather than dragged along with the garments.

The ten pieces read as ONE capsule when the range grid puts them adjacent: one ground, one white point, one warmth, one piece height in frame. A frame that cannot be brought to the set is named in the note, not shipped at eighty percent.
Every hardware crop contains the whole of the piece it depicts, and no reference card, bench edge or prop appears in any delivered frame.
The lookbook's per-look pages read as the season's muted world on the delivered document, on every page and not only the first one.
Every cut-out is whole. The cut edge holds on the dark pieces at full resolution on our own colour, with the shoulder seam, the placket and the hem intact and nothing bitten away.
Every supplied asset is listed in the delivery manifest as used, reference-only, superseded, or rejected with a concrete reason; no input disappears silently.
Final files open successfully, use unambiguous names, match the stated dimensions and formats, and include editable sources only where the scoped deliverable requires them.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns handsome pictures of workwear. IDENTITY: these are this workshop's actual ten pieces in their actual fabrics and colourways, with the actual hardware they cast, and the crest belongs to a real club that is lending it, so a regenerated garment is a garment they do not sell and a regenerated crest is somebody else's badge on a partner's tag. SPEC: forty stockists need a linesheet whose price grid is a real table, whole cut-outs that hold on the house colour, and a hang-tag run whose page count equals the row count at print resolution with each tag carrying its own row's picture, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the shoppable set and the lookbook are defined by being editable, because the capsule sells through and pieces drop out mid-season, and a ten person workshop cannot re-commission each time. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did this cut find an edge on the charcoal, is this file the piece its name claims, did the season's tone survive the import.

proof: Every required operation is present in the captured 99-tool ChatGPT Adobe inventory.
The client brief is host-neutral; connector-specific scoring is isolated in connector_profile and verifier_contract.
Artifact acceptance never depends on a raw connector response field.
Unsupported truth, fabrication, press, legal, or color claims have an explicit defer or disclose state.
residual_limits: Express work is template adaptation, not unrestricted canvas authoring.
Quick Cut is used only for visually led selection and never as semantic speech editing.
Automatic vectorization does not independently establish fabrication readiness.
Interactive Acrobat page-organization operations are excluded from zero-human execution.

acceptance_bar_note: The acceptance bar applies only to the scoped deliverables above. Hidden defects and connector quirks remain benchmark-internal and are not leaked into the client-facing brief.
